sanskrit_verse:
पलाण्डुं विड्वराहं च छत्राकं ग्रामकुक्कुटम् ।
लशुनं गृञ्जनं चैव जग्ध्वा चान्द्रायणं चरेत् ॥१७६॥
transliteration: palāṇḍuṃ viḍvarāhaṃ ca chatrākaṃ grāmakukkuṭam | laśunaṃ gṛñjanaṃ caiva jagdhvā cāndrāyaṇaṃ caret || 176 ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Having consumed onion, boar's flesh, mushrooms, village poultry, garlic, or mustard, one shall perform the Cāndrāyaṇa vow.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority: The embodied being holds responsibility commensurate with conscious choice.
Causation: Ingestion directly conditions energetic and spiritual misalignment.
Capacity-based responsibility: Restoration is required when volitional intake disrupts dharmic equilibrium.
Restoration logic: Ritual observance realigns consciousness with cosmic order.
Consciousness alignment: Purification through vow restores innate divinity.
executable_legal_axioms: IF (agent.consumes ∈ {palāṇḍu, viḍvarāha, chatrāka, grāmakukkuṭa, laśuna, gṛñjana}) THEN agent.perform_cāndrāyaṇa()
supreme_court_application: In adjudication, the threshold of responsibility is established by voluntary ingestion. The court must verify intent and awareness, then direct completion of the vow as a constitutional restorative mechanism, bypassing punitive frameworks.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa confirms that ingestion creates sequential energetic distortion. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows that purification follows causal intake. Responsibility is proportional to awareness and choice. Non-punitive reality is upheld as the vow realigns consciousness without infliction of harm.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Verify energetic recalibration post-vow via consciousness resonance scan.
Reintegrate individual into dharmic community upon vow fulfillment.
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law is executed. Dharma is restored. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness is the Supreme Adjudicator.
